title: Grewingk Lake topobathy, first attempt (ice as of 19 Sep 2023), 2 m
note: First Grewingk Lake topobathy, Hig's request of 2026-10-13: the lake bed from the levelled 2023 multibeam (grewingk_sonar_2023) where it exists, everything else in the lake from the fill's lake basin conditioned by every sounding (Ed Berg's 2017 sounder track, Hig's lead-line drops 2017/2019/2021/2026), the shores from Grewingk 2021 lidar, and the GLACIER as Mark Laker's SfM of 19 September 2023 shows it (dixon_2023; ice = the 2020 G10040 outline minus what the lake had taken by 2023, make_ice.py). Hig's two rules: the ICE FACE is vertical and puts no constraint on the depth (fill: ice_face 'free' -- no shore taper, no fixed value, the basin runs into the face), and the bed is 150 m deep in the middle of the lake (fill: lake_dmax 150 m for the Grewingk Lake domain, in place of the Hollister / glacial-scaling estimate). Lower bounds (lines that ran out) are not used yet. as_of = the SfM date.

layers.name: ctx3dep
layers.notes: Fallback everywhere: USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second seamless (~10 m; IfSAR-derived in Alaska), the same data Mapterhorn serves in Alaska (median difference 0 m against this bake, reference_mapterhorn) -- read locally rather than from Mapterhorn's tiles. NAVD88. Date a nominal 2012 (IfSAR era); sigma 3 m, so any survey outranks it and it shows only where nothing else does. Its lakes are hydroflattened: class ground here, so where it is the only data a lake reads as a flat surface -- the class axis from the surveys above still says water there.
layers.class_notes: Stands in only where no survey of the stack has a cell (no footprint rasters: the 2021 class raster is ~60% void over this box).

layers.name: grewingk2021
layers.notes: shift_m +0.36: MEASURED 2026-10-10, not from metadata. On bare smooth flat ground (both DTMs < 0.05 m rough, slope < 3 deg, 2-20 m: beaches, flats, fans) KBay 2023 reads +0.36 m above Grewingk 2021 with NMAD 0.06 m (n 108k at 2 m), while KBay reads +0.014 m (NMAD 0.048) against Seldovia 2019 NCMP topobathy, the survey the 2009 bathymetry's MLLW->NAVD88 shift was tied to, and the reclass matches the vendor DEM to 1 cm. Two independent products against one: Grewingk sits ~0.36 m low in the collection's NAVD88(GEOID12B) frame despite its metadata. No third witness overlaps it (Homer 2019 and Lower Kenai have no data over it). Belongs in datasets.json as vertical_shift_m for hosting to apply after its own check; applied here explicitly so the test composite has no 0.4 m seam at Grewingk's edge.
layers.class_notes: Ground wherever the DGGS DTM has a value, WATER where the 2021 point classification says so (obs/grewingk_2021_lakes, which is ~60% void over this box, so only its water is used), ICE inside the 2020 glacier outline. DTM cells over the lake that the point classes miss read ground at the water level; the fill drops lake observations within lake_surface_tol_m of the level as surface, not evidence. WATER also wherever the DTM is the flat lake surface (48.55 +- 0.35 m, connected to the point-class lake; make_ice.py lake_2021.tif): without it the lake surface read ground along the ice face, and the fill saw a shore at water level between the lake and the ice. In the retreat zone (lake by 2023, ice in the 2020 outline) the 2021 ice surface is classed WATER: classed ice it still won there under a water class_now (sequential rules), standing the old ice in for the lake bed.

layers.name: dixon2023
layers.notes: Mark Laker's SfM DSM (USFWS, dixon_2023), 19 Sep 2023, NAVD88 converted, read from make_ice.py's copy that holds ONLY the 2023 ice and the retreat zone (the lake gained from the 2020 outline): ICE on the tongue, WATER in the retreat zone. Nowhere else -- SfM is poor over water and at the lake shore (Hig, 2026-10-13; here NMAD 2.9 m over the lake, +3.4 m above the lidar on land beside it), and given everywhere it became the newest class over the lake.

layers.name: fill
layers.notes: The hole interpolation (composite.py fill, topobathy/fill.py): a context-aware prior (shore bands from the rim slope, low-tide floor) conditioned by the soundings. Class modelled, so it stands in at half rank under water/bed and never where a real observation exists; sigma from fill_sigma.tif (grows from the shore, relaxes near soundings). Optional: skipped until the fill has been run; 'composite.py fill' treats the cells it won as holes, so build -> fill -> build is idempotent.

lake_dmax.why: Hig 2026-10-13: 150 m deep in the middle of the lake
lake_dmax.level_why: the 12 Oct 2021 lidar water surface (flat at 48.55 m). The 2023 SfM water reads 51.6 m median but scatters NMAD 2.9 m (p5-p95 48-58 m) and stands +3.4 m above the lidar even on land near the lake: not a level.

fill.notes: Sparse depths: a dated export of the soundings database (Grewingk: Berg 2017 sounder, thinned; Higman lead line 2017/2019/2021/2026; z = each survey's level - depth). ice_face 'free': rim cells classed ice are neither shore (no slope extension, no taper of the basin) nor fixed boundary values (residual and spline free there). lake_dmax: the basin's deepest point fixed by Hig instead of estimated.
fill.channel_notes: Channel detection off for this box (channel_min_m2 huge): it read the deep east end of Grewingk Lake, by the ice face, as a river channel and gave it a shallow channel bed (first fill, 2026-10-13).
